claims.claim: The ten presuppositions of science (objective world, knowability, truth, logic, cognitive reliability, language adequacy, uniformity of nature, validity of mathematics, moral integrity, comprehensibility) cannot be proven by science itself and are more at home in a theistic worldview than a naturalistic one.
claims.plain_english: Science has to assume certain things to work—like the world being real and understandable—but it can't prove those assumptions. Those assumptions make more sense if God exists than if everything is just matter.
claims.evidence_given: References Hugh Gauch's work on scientific method in biblical context and Hans Albert's Münchhausen Trilemma. Argues that these axioms are 'theological truths' describing a universe from a rational mind.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a naturalistic worldview could provide a non-circular, non-regressive justification for all ten presuppositions without borrowing from theism.

claims.claim: The Coherence Equation dC/dt = O·G(1−C) − S·C is a formal differential equation that describes how moral coherence evolves in any system governed by moral law, derived from thermodynamics, population dynamics, and information theory.
claims.plain_english: There's a math equation that predicts how moral order in a society changes over time. It comes from three different fields of science that all point to the same formula.
claims.evidence_given: Claims derivation from three independent domains producing the same mathematical form. States formal verification in Lean 4 (3 files, 942 lines, zero sorry). Provides historical case studies as empirical support.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the equation fails to predict outcomes in new historical cases, or if the derivation from the three domains is shown to be mathematically flawed or not truly independent.

claims.claim: When a society suppresses a moral evil by force alone without providing an alternative pathway (grace), the Coherence Equation predicts collapse, substitution, or underground persistence; when grace operates, it predicts sustainable transformation.
claims.plain_english: If you just ban something bad without offering people a better way, things get worse. But if you also provide a positive alternative, real change happens. The math equation says so.
claims.evidence_given: Five historical case studies: Prohibition (1920-1933), Soviet Atheism (1917-1991), Victorian England (1837-1901), War on Drugs (1971-Present), Cultural Revolution (1966-1976). Claims pattern is structural, not coincidental.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a historical case of pure suppression (no grace pathway) resulted in sustainable moral improvement, or if a grace-operated reform failed to produce sustainable transformation.

claims.claim: The unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics in the natural sciences (Wigner's puzzle) has no explanation within physics itself and points to a metaphysical ground—the Logos—as the explanation for why reality is intelligible to the human mind.
claims.plain_english: Nobody can explain why math works so perfectly to describe the universe. Physics can't answer this. The best explanation is that reality is built on a rational, personal foundation—what the Bible calls the Word or Logos.
claims.evidence_given: Cites Eugene Wigner's 1960 paper. Argues that the question 'why does mathematics describe reality?' is not a physics question but a metaphysics question. Links to John 1:1-3 and the concept of Logos.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a purely naturalistic explanation for the effectiveness of mathematics were found that did not require a rational ground, or if mathematics were shown to be a human invention that only approximately describes reality.

claims.claim: The multiverse hypothesis does not explain fine-tuning because the multiverse itself requires fine-tuning, pushing the question back one level without answering it, and it is metaphysics dressed in equations, not science.
claims.plain_english: Saying 'there are infinite universes, so one had to be just right' doesn't solve the problem. You'd need to explain why the multiverse itself has the right laws to produce universes. Plus, it's not real science—it's a guess.
claims.evidence_given: Presented as part of the 'Four Moves' argument structure (Move 3). Argues that the multiverse is not testable and requires its own fine-tuning.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a multiverse model were developed that required no fine-tuning of its own laws, or if empirical evidence for a multiverse were found that did not rely on untestable assumptions.

claims.claim: The formal verification in Lean 4 of the Coherence Equation and related theorems (substrate priority, entropy repair, C ≠ χ distinction, Grace Operator, adversarial discriminator) constitutes a genuine formal proof that theism passes a gate that false-positive candidates (pantheism, deism, simulation) fail.
claims.plain_english: A computer proof-checker has verified that the math behind this framework is logically sound. It also shows that other worldviews like pantheism or deism don't fit the same logical structure, but theism does.
claims.evidence_given: States 3 files, 942 lines, zero sorry in Lean 4. Describes specific theorems: substrate priority, product collapse, entropy repair, C ≠ chi, grace preserves coherence, adversarial discriminator. Acknowledges Lean does not verify metaphysical correspondence.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a false-positive control (pantheism, deism, simulation) were shown to pass the same formal gate under the same definitions, or if the formal definitions were shown to be inconsistent with the intended metaphysical claims.

claims.claim: The 'alien standard'—that the designer must be other, not a cosmic engineer but a being whose nature explains why reality is rational, moral, and personal—is not a conclusion but a precondition; surrender is required before reasoning works.
claims.plain_english: To understand God, you can't just think your way to Him. You have to first give up control and surrender. Then, and only then, does reasoning about God actually work. This isn't anti-intellectual—it's how the system is set up.
claims.evidence_given: Presented as 'Move 4—The Keystone' in the Four Moves argument. Described as 'Theophysics Axiom Zero.' Argues that posture is part of the experiment when the observer is part of the system.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a purely rational, non-surrender-based argument could conclusively prove the existence and nature of the theistic God, or if the claim that surrender is a precondition were shown to be arbitrary or falsifiable.

claims.claim: The convergence of independent lines of evidence from independent fields using independent methods (logic, mathematics, history, data, lived experience) arriving at the same conclusion is itself the evidence for the theistic framework, not decoration.
claims.plain_english: It's not just one argument that points to God. It's many different arguments from many different areas of study—math, history, personal experience—all pointing in the same direction. That convergence is the real proof.
claims.evidence_given: Lists multiple domains: Gauch's presuppositions, Münchhausen Trilemma, Coherence Equation, five historical case studies, three grace-success cases (Thuggee, foot-binding, dueling), Lean verification, adversarial discriminator. Claims the convergence is not coincidence.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the independent lines of evidence were shown to be not truly independent (e.g., all relying on the same flawed assumption), or if a naturalistic framework could produce an equally strong convergence from independent domains.

claims.claim: The 'why' question cannot be amputated from scientific inquiry without measurable consequences: when the system closes, when the state enforces without restoring, when the method stops at 'brute fact,' coherence decays measurably in historical systems.
claims.plain_english: If you try to do science or run a society without asking 'why'—just focusing on 'how'—things fall apart. History shows this. The math equation predicts it. You can't ignore the deeper questions without paying a price.
claims.evidence_given: References the five historical case studies as empirical signature of what happens when the why is suppressed. Links to the Coherence Equation prediction that dC/dt = −S·C when O = 0 (no ordering force).
claims.what_would_break_it: If a society successfully suppressed moral evil through force alone without grace and achieved sustainable long-term coherence, or if a purely naturalistic worldview produced greater societal coherence than a theistic one.

claims.claim: Theophysics is not another argument added to the pile (like Swinburne, Meyer, Plantinga, Craig, Longmire) but a unified formalism that explains why the arguments converge and predicts where the next convergence will appear.
claims.plain_english: This isn't just one more reason to believe in God. It's a whole new way of thinking that shows why all the other reasons point in the same direction—and it can even predict where new evidence will show up.
claims.evidence_given: Compares to Swinburne (probability), Meyer (biological information), Plantinga (epistemology), Craig (kalam), Longmire (consilience). Claims Theophysics uses differential equations (stronger formalism), argues from mathematical structure itself, shows naturalism undermines its own mathematics, formalizes convergence.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the claimed unified formalism were shown to be reducible to existing arguments, or if it failed to make novel predictions that could be tested, or if the mathematical structure were shown to be inconsistent with the claimed convergence.
